name: Mercedes-Benz OM617 3.0 L inline-5 diesel
statusNote: Primary OMOBD development engine. Firmware support exists for every capability marked 'proposed'; none has been validated on a running OM617 yet.

identification.source: General reference knowledge; not checked against Mercedes-Benz documentation in this repository. Confirm with the engine number stamped on the block and the factory service manual.
identification.injectionNote: Bosch inline injection pump with mechanical governor. There is no engine ECU and no factory OBD system: OMOBD's OBD-style PIDs are synthetic.

variants.label: OM617.95x Turbo Diesel
variants.variantNote: Turbo variants are commonly listed as OM617.950, .951 and .952 for different chassis. Use your stamped number.

egt.note: K-type probe in the exhaust manifold collector ahead of the turbine (turbo) or in the manifold outlet (NA). MAX31855 preferred: MAX6675 has a lower ceiling and no fault detail.

boost.note: Absolute MAP sensor teed into the intake manifold. Boost is CALCULATED as MAP minus the atmospheric reference.

vacuum.note: Absolute sensor teed into the vacuum system (pump outlet, reservoir, or an actuator line). Vacuum depth is calculated from the atmospheric reference. A 15-115 kPa sensor would give better resolution but is not yet in preOBD's library.

coolantTemp.note: Use a separate, immersed sender. Do not share the factory gauge sender: two loads on one sender change both readings. The factory sender's resistance curve is not characterised in this repository.

oilTemp.note: Immersed sender via a sandwich adapter at the oil filter or a drilled/tapped drain plug. Surface-mounted probes read low and lag; see docs/hardware/SENSOR_COMPATIBILITY.md.

transTemp.note: Optional. Fitting depends on the transmission (factory Mercedes automatic, or the conversion's transmission).

oilPressure.note: Add a sender on a tee; keep the factory gauge line. RPM-dependent low-pressure advisory available once you enter a validated curve.

fuelPressure.note: Low-pressure supply side only (lift pump to injection pump). NEVER connect a sensor to the high-pressure injection lines.

engineHours.note: Calculated: time with measured RPM at or above the running threshold. Needs an RPM input.

vehicleSpeed.note: Depends on the vehicle, not the engine. Factory Mercedes speedometers of this era are often cable driven: a hall sensor or a transmission/transfer-case VSS is needed.

fuelFlow.note: Not implemented. Diesel return flow makes a single flow meter wrong: supply and return must both be measured. Any consumption figure would be an ESTIMATE and must be labelled as such.

factoryEcuDiagnostics.note: The OM617 has no ECU. OMOBD never reports ECU fault codes for it.

rpmSources.note: Alternator W (phase) terminal through a conditioning circuit (docs/hardware/SIGNAL_CONDITIONING.md). Calibrate pole count and pulley ratio against a known tachometer. Not every alternator has a W terminal.

Where a factory tachometer is fitted, its signal source and pulses per revolution vary by chassis and year and are not documented here. Measure the signal with an oscilloscope before connecting anything.
A magnetic (VR) pickup needs a VR interface IC; a hall sensor needs only level shifting. Set pulses per revolution from the trigger tooth count.

thresholds._note: Every value is null until validated for YOUR engine. OMOBD's configs ship with no alarm rules: preOBD's generic preset limits are not OM617 specifications.

boostMaxBar.note: Depends on turbo, wastegate and ALDA settings.

oilPressureCurve.note: Enter rpm/minBar points from the service manual into OMOBD settings (oilCurve).

interfaces.for: resistive senders (with bias resistors) and 0.5-4.5 V sensors (with dividers)
fused, ignition-switched, automotive buck converter with reverse and transient protection
